facts.value: The following documents are required for application to the Master of Science in Business Administration: proof of a bachelor's degree in a business-related field with at least 90 ECTS in business science modules; proof of English language skills; a current resume; a copy of the university entrance qualification (e.g., high school diploma); proof of passing the DSH-2 exam for international applicants.
A bachelor's degree in a business-related field or a related field is required.
At least 90 ECTS must be obtained in business science modules.
A minimum language level of B2 according to the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR) is required.

Proof can be provided by a bachelor's degree fully conducted in English, a standardized language test with evidence of level B2, an English course at the university with explicit indication of level B2, or high school diploma if English was taken until graduation.

The following proofs are not accepted: semester abroad, individual English-speaking modules in bachelor's studies, language courses at the university without specified level, and CET-4 or CET-6 (Chinese language tests).

Examples of accepted language tests include: Cambridge Certificate (First Certificate in English A-C), DAAD Language Certificate (B2), IELTS Academic (minimum 5.0), LCCI (EFB Level 3), TOEFL (minimum 72), TOEIC (minimum 785), UNIcert (UNIcert II).
The TOEFL code for electronic submission is B073.
If the examination board has doubts about the English language skills of an applicant, admission may be granted with the condition of obtaining a TOEFL test by a certain deadline.
A simple copy of the university entrance qualification (e.g., high school diploma) is required.
International applicants must prove having passed the DSH-2 exam within the application period.

Applicants with TestDaF results (all results with at least TDN 4), Goethe Certificate C2, KMK Examination: German Language Diploma Second Stage (DSD II), and certain other qualifications may be exempt from the DSH-2 exam.
Applicants with German language skills at B1/B2/C1 can apply for a preparatory course for the DSH-2 exam. Admission to the preparatory course does not grant admission to the master's program.
Applicants who completed their bachelor's studies in Vietnam, the People's Republic of China, or India require an APS certificate from the Academic Examination Office.
